quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose their grip and your vehicle slides on a layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian knows you are there.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian. Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: If a bus signals to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to rejoin the road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, what helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to improve grip.
Leave highways as quickly as possible.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. This and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: Which factors affect how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: All three factors
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication.

questions.question: A "Reduced speed, 35 mph" sign means:

options.text: The new 35 mph limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph limit starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down.
Reduce to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A reduced speed sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians of danger. Sound it if another driver might hit you.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts normal traffic flow
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts normal traffic flow
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block normal traffic. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when visibility drops to 500 feet or less. Do not use high beams in fog—they reflect back and reduce visibility.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children:

options.text: Do not move until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel too confident, and causes more driving mistakes.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.
questions.explanation: If you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beams. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can see the road ahead clearly.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can see the road ahead clearly, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines are doubled in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of low clearance ahead.

questions.question: While backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head so you can see through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. Driving safely may require you to go slower than the posted limit. When conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or shows a green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or shows a green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Do not move until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.

questions.question: When must you stop for a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of your car.
Only if there is a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Stop for pedestrians at any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked. Let them cross safely before you drive.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway when entering from a private road.

questions.question: What does a green arrow and a red light at the same time mean?

options.text: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
Wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. Make sure the intersection is clear first.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to surprises.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, then proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What is the correct order of colors on a traffic light from top to bottom?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom. When lights are horizontal, red is on the left and green on the right.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard right away. Grip the wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Release the gas and slow down gradually. Once you are going very slowly, brake lightly and move off the road safely.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without hard braking and carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for traffic before re-entering.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: What do flashing amber lights on a school bus mean?

options.text: The bus has finished loading or unloading children.
The bus is about to stop to load or unload children. Be ready to stop.
The bus is broken down on the side of the road. You may pass carefully.
The bus is loading or unloading children. You may go slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus is about to stop to load or unload children. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Flashing amber lights warn that the bus is about to stop to load or unload children. Get ready to stop. When red lights flash, stop before reaching the bus and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle while driving?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop in these situations: at a stop sign, at a red light, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops use time and fuel to speed back up. Look ahead while driving. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.
